findings.title: RC4 manifest omits the deprecated approved graph
findings.trigger: A consumer uses the RC4 manifest to verify that the graph moved to `deprecated/` without byte changes.
findings.consequence: The manifest provides no binding for the deprecated graph, so the required manifest-based preservation proof cannot be performed.
findings.evidence: `release_candidate/rc4/manifest.v1.json` lines 18–78 list the snapshot files but contain no `deprecated/implementation.graph.v4.yaml` entry. The live file independently hashes to the expected digest, but that digest is absent from the manifest as T18 explicitly requires.

observations: The validator returned `valid: true`; 120 tests passed, while 13 temporary-file mutation tests were deselected because the review sandbox prohibits all writes.

Each embedded code block contains one additional trailing blank line relative to its live source, so the raw fenced-body hashes differ from the manifest hashes; the substantive embedded content is otherwise identical.
reasoning: The schema/contract bindings, five live digest recomputations, model assignments, graph changes, prompt renames, historical hashes, and validator wiring survived review. The live deprecated graph has the correct approved digest, but PKGV2-T18 specifically requires that digest to be recorded in the RC4 manifest, where the file is omitted entirely. That unconditional criterion failure determines the verdict.
